newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: MEAT CONTAMINATION BEING INVESTIGATED
Health authorities in Victoria and South Australia are investigating the source of meat contamination which has led to the deaths of an elderly Victorian man and woman.
A 79-year-old man and 86-year-old woman have died from salmonella poisoning, and 22 other Victorians and eight South Australians are ill with symptoms of salmonella poisoning.

Largo Smallgoods in the Melbourne suburb of Reservoir is a possible source of contamination, but this has NOT been confirmed, and not alL of the cases of salmonella poisoning are necessarily linked to Largo products.
Lago has begun a recall of corned silverside, virginian ham and easy-cut ham.
People with any of these goods from the Lago factory, dated before March the 14th are being advised NOT to eat them.
The Health Department says sliced ham and corned beef made after that date are not contaminated.
FINANCIAL SIDE OF PREMIER'S CONFERENCE SET TO WIND UP
The financial aspect of the Premiers Conference in Canberra is due to wind up soon, with the States apparently prepared to accept a cut of around one per cent in their tied grants.
The Prime Minster's told State and Territory leaders the Commonwealth has to continue its policy of tight fiscal constraint if the economy is to continue improving.
There are concerns from some States that the Government is trying to make cuts in other ways, such as asking them to match the environment funding in the natural heritage trust dollar for dollar.
Their main worry is the health system, telling the Federal Government its private health insurance rebate isn't enough to fix the problem.
And they're backing a plan to continue the extra medicare levy that was brought in to pay for the gun buyback scheme, in order to provide another 500-million dollars for the public health system.
COURT, BORBIDGE OPPOSED TO PM'S WIK RESPONSE
State leaders appear to be divided over the direction the Prime Minister's taking in his response to the Wik decision.
Western Australia and Queensland are opposed to a proposal put forward by John Howard, with WA Premier Richard Court saying it's unacceptable.
No details are yet available on the Prime Minister's response.
Mr Court has been supported by Queensland leader Rob Borbidge, who's warned of serious consequences for John Howard's Government if the Nationals aren't satisfied with the outcome.
However New South Wales Premier Bob Carr says justice for Aborigines must remain paramount, while Victoria's Jeff Kennett is right behind the Prime Minsiter's efforts.
BROWN SAYS LATE NIGHT VOTE NO GOOD FOR ANYONE
Greens Senator Bob Brown says holding next week's vital euthansia vote in the Senate in the dead of night, is in nobody's interests.
Voting on the private members bill that seeks to override the Northern Territory's voluntary euthanasia laws, will begin after nine-o-clock on Monday night.
Senator Brown says staging the final stage of the debate at such a late hour will mean it's inaccessible to much of the listening public.
HMAS MELBOURNE TRYING TO RECOVER BEACON
HMAS Melbourne is trying to recover an emergency positioning beacon from the missing new Zealand yacht, Queen Charlotte.
A major air and sea search is underway for the five crew members of the yacht, which is thought to have sunk in rough weather, in the Coral Sea.
Search co-ordinator Daryl Hiron says an aircraft has also located some more debris near the beacon, but there is no sign of a life-raft.
SAVVAS PLEADS GUILTY TO ESCAPING
Convicted drug dealer George Savvas has pleaded guilty in a Sydney court to escaping from a maximum security prison in southern New South Wales last year
The 46-year-old appeared in court this morning following his arrest overnight at a Japanese resturant in central Sydney. -- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
